description:
`analyze_activation` re-runs once per callee-return ascent, and nothing dedupes
those re-runs across scheduler rounds. The design question -- whether a
cone-settled re-analysis rung is the right shape -- is still open and still
correct. What is NOT usable is its acceptance criterion.

## Premise verified at main 417c5b0b5

- `prepare_function_call` is now jobs/semantic.rs:1768, and the ordinary
  per-callee subscription is at :1785:

      // The read is the subscription that re-wakes this caller when the
      // callee's return evidence rises -- chaotic iteration needs no wait here,
      // so mutual recursion cannot deadlock.
      reads.push(FactKey::ReturnType(activation.clone()));

  So the CRITICAL CONSTRAINT stands and is now documented at the read site:
  callers READ, never WAIT, so a coarse cone-settled fact the caller WAITS on can
  never settle.
- The cross-round batching gap is intact: `coalesced_seen` is a `HashSet` created
  fresh inside ONE `complete()` batch (scheduler.rs:302) and consulted only in
  `enqueue_step` (:383-392). It cannot dedupe across sequential callee
  completions on different rounds.
- The model to mirror still exists: `settle_demand_cone`
  (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:563, called from :370).
- `analyze_activation` (jobs/semantic.rs:65) is still one Job publishing many
  heterogeneous facts, so the obstacle sizing stands.

Churn is still observable, slightly smaller than the old baseline. On
00001_quicksort_plus_foo: AnalyzeActivation 67 spans (old baseline 72) against 18
executables. On 00181_enum_reduce_operator_ref: 46 (old baseline 45), 12
executables.

## THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS UNBUILDABLE AS WRITTEN

The old ticket says "return_type.defined telemetry now carries changed:bool", and
its whole step (5) depends on it. IT DOES NOT.
`World::define_activation_return` (world.rs:2835-2850) emits the event ONLY when
it changed:

    if outcome.changed { self.emit_world_key(&["fz","compiler2","return_type","defined"], key); }

There is no `changed` measurement on the event. `define_callsite_summary`
(world.rs:2852-2858) is the same shape. So "return_type 1 changed / 22 unchanged"
and "callsite.defined 136 total (59 changed / 77 unchanged)" are not measurable
at HEAD by any means.

Worse: none of `return_type.defined`, `activation_analysis.defined` or
`callsite.defined` reach the `--log-telemetry` JSONL sink AT ALL. A full run of
00001 emitted 1041 events, entirely accounted for by pull.product.settled (540),
compiler2.job spans (480), lexer (12), demand.cone.settled (2),
backend_program.defined (2), pull.session.finished (2), diag.warning (2),
runtime.process_exited (1).

## Precursor, before the arc can start

Re-land a MEASURABLE churn signal: either restore `changed` as a measurement on
`return_type.defined`, or route the world-key events to the public sink. Without
it there is no way to prove the arc did anything.

Note this is the same instrumentation gap fz-kdt.13 hits from the other side --
the `fz.compiler2.job` span carries only `kind`, no activation key, so
per-activation fire counts are not derivable either. One fix serves both.

## Line drift

semantic.rs:1562 -> jobs/semantic.rs:1768; semantic.rs:78-83 -> the comment now
at jobs/semantic.rs:1782-1784; semantic.rs:66-262 -> jobs/semantic.rs:65;
scheduler.rs:180,249 -> scheduler.rs:302 and :390;
runtime_demand.rs:286-323 -> jobs/runtime_demand.rs:563.
title: Collapse cross-round AnalyzeActivation re-runs; its telemetry acceptance criterion does not exist and must be re-landed first
